samples.summary: Unsetting `nf` across the whole selection destroys other cells' number formats (currency/date/percent)
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` derives `keys = nf === 'number' ? ['dp','nf'] : ['dp']` from the ACTIVE cell only (sheet.ts:4196-4207), then `unsetRangeStyleKeys(keys)` deletes those keys from every owned layer and from `cell.s` of every cell in the selection (sheet.ts:4315-4335, removeCellStyleKeysInRange 4343-4372). Example: select A1:B1 where A1 = '1.5' with cell style {nf:'number', dp:2} (active) and B1 has {nf:'currency', cu:'USD', dp:2}. Decrease decimals: target 1 === valueDp(A1) 1 and nf==='number', so keys=['dp','nf']; the ownership guard (4242-4277) only rejects layers OUTSIDE the selection, so B1's own cell style is stripped and B1 silently loses its currency format (same for a 'date'-formatted neighbour stamped by setData). A key set chosen from one cell must not be unset from cells that never had that format.

samples.summary: Decrease/increase decimals can change other cells' displayed precision because the unset decision uses only the active cell's `valueDp`
samples.evidence: `const { dp, nf, valueDp, explicitDp } = await this.getActiveDecimalState()` (4196) and `if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable)` (4203) test the ACTIVE cell's raw-value precision but the resulting unset applies to the whole selection. Concretely: A1='1.5', A2='1.2345', select A1:A2. Decrease → writes {dp:0, nf:'number'} for both (shows 2 / 1). Increase → dp=0 explicit, target 1 === valueDp(A1)=1, nf='number' → all dp/nf removed → A1 renders '1.5' (intended) but A2 jumps back to '1.2345', i.e. pressing *increase by one decimal* moved A2 from 0 to 4 decimals. The old code wrote an explicit uniform dp and had no such divergence.

samples.summary: Comment/assumption that dropping `nf:'number'` keeps the cell looking the same is false — grouping separators are lost
samples.evidence: Lines 4204-4207 justify removing `nf` with "the cell keeps looking the same", but `formatValue(value,'number',dp)` goes through `toLocaleString` (format.ts:127-130) which adds thousands separators, while plain format returns the raw string verbatim (format.ts:111-113). For value '1234.5': with {nf:'number',dp:1} the cell shows '1,234.5'; after the unset it shows '1234.5'. The new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:89-92 encodes exactly this lossy outcome (`toBe('1234.5')`). So decrease-then-increase on a number-formatted cell silently drops the user's number format and its grouping.

samples.summary: Empty style objects are left behind at sheet/column/row level, so `getStyle` returns `{}` instead of `undefined`
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` returns `{}` (not undefined) when every key is removed (range-styles.ts:64-76); the sheet/col/row branches only test `if (next)` (4283, 4294, 4306) and therefore write and cache empty style objects (`this.colStyles.set(col, {})`, `store.setColumnStyle(col, {})`). `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:883-884) treats a truthy `{}` as a present layer, so `getStyle` now returns `{}` rather than `undefined` for every cell in that column, and an empty style node is persisted to the document. The range-patch branch (4324) and the cell branch (4367) correctly drop empties; these three do not — contradicting the change's own 'leaves nothing behind' goal. The new test at decimals.test.ts:193-195 only asserts `style?.dp`/`style?.nf` are undefined, so it passes with the residue in place.

samples.summary: `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` rewrites cells through `compactCell`, dropping spill metadata
samples.evidence: `const nextCell = compactCell(existing, next); ... await this.store.set(anchor, nextCell)` (4366-4370). `compactCell` copies only `v`, `f` and `s` (style-mutation.ts:57-69), while `Cell` also carries `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor` and `spillBlocked` (model/core/types.ts:209-217). Decreasing decimals over a spill anchor or a spilled ghost cell that happens to carry a style therefore erases its spill bookkeeping, corrupting spill rendering/blocking state. The same lossy pattern exists in `clearCellStylesInRange`/`setStyle`, so it is pre-existing, but this change adds a new user-reachable path to it.

samples.summary: `target < 0` early return makes decrease a no-op for the whole selection based on the active cell alone
samples.evidence: `if (target < 0) { return; }` (4198-4200) replaces the previous `Math.max(0, dp - 1)` clamp. With a selection whose active cell is empty/text (dp inferred 0) but whose other cells carry dp: 3, pressing Decrease now does nothing at all instead of lowering the other cells, because the decision comes solely from `getActiveDecimalState()`.

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` counts characters after the first dot for non-numeric text too
samples.evidence: `const dotIndex = value.indexOf('.'); return dotIndex >= 0 ? value.length - dotIndex - 1 : 0;` — for a text cell 'v1.2.3' this returns 3 and for '12.5kg' returns 3. That number is now not only the starting dp (pre-existing) but also the equality target that decides whether an explicit style is removed (`target === valueDp`, sheet.ts:4203), so garbage precision from text values now drives a destructive unset.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. changeDecimals derives the unset key set from the ACTIVE cell only (sheet.ts:4196-4207, via getActiveDecimalState at 4165-4186 which reads getStyle(this.activeCell)), including 'nf' when the active cell's format is 'number'. unsetRangeStyleKeys then applies those keys to the entire selection: rangeStyles patches contained in the selection are stripped (4315-4331) and removeCellStyleKeysInRange deletes the keys from cell.s of every populated cell in every target range with no per-cell format check (4343-4372). The conflict guard at 4242-4277 only rejects layers the selection does NOT own (sheet/col/row outside selection, or intersecting-but-not-contained range patches), so it does not protect a neighbouring cell inside the selection whose own style has nf:'currency'/'date'/'percent'. Per-cell nf is really stored (setRangeStyle -> applyStylePatchToExistingCells, 3736-3742; CellStyle.nf/cu/dp at model/core/types.ts:99-101), and the UI path has no homogeneity check (view/spreadsheet.ts:534-549 only guards !sheet/_readOnly). Result: decreasing decimals on a mixed-format selection silently destroys other cells' number formats — reachable format/data loss, major under the correctness rubric. Existing tests (test/sheet/decimals.test.ts) only use nf:'number', so nothing guards this.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `getActiveDecimalState` (sheet.ts:4165-4186) computes `valueDp`/`explicitDp` solely from `this.activeCell`, while `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4196-4217) uses that single-cell state at line 4203 to decide to call `unsetRangeStyleKeys(['dp','nf'])`, which strips the keys from owned range patches and from every cell in the whole selection (sheet.ts:4315-4335, 4343-4373). With a mixed-precision selection (A1='1.5', A2='1.2345', active A1) a Decrease writes {dp:0, nf:'number'} to both, and the following Increase satisfies `explicitDp && target===valueDp && inheritable` for A1 and unsets dp/nf for both cells. format.ts:111-113 returns the raw string when no format is set and format.ts:124-131 renders nf:'number' at `dp` decimals, so A2 visibly jumps from 0 to 4 decimals on a single 'increase by one decimal' action. No guard restricts the unset path to single-cell or uniform-precision selections (the only bail-out at sheet.ts:4242-4277 concerns unowned style layers), and the design docs (sheet-style.md:200-224, the todo doc) describe only single-cell round-trip semantics, so this is not documented intended behavior. Real, reachable, user-visible logic bug in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Comment/assumption that dropping `nf:'number'` keeps the cell looking the same is false — grouping separators are lost
finding.evidence: Lines 4204-4207 justify removing `nf` with "the cell keeps looking the same", but `formatValue(value,'number',dp)` goes through `toLocaleString` (format.ts:127-130) which adds thousands separators, while plain format returns the raw string verbatim (format.ts:111-113). For value '1234.5': with {nf:'number',dp:1} the cell shows '1,234.5'; after the unset it shows '1234.5'. The new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:89-92 encodes exactly this lossy outcome (`toBe('1234.5')`). So decrease-then-increase on a number-formatted cell silently drops the user's number format and its grouping.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: sheet.ts:4202-4211 unsets both `dp` and `nf` whenever `nf === 'number'` and `target === valueDp`, justified by a comment claiming the cell "keeps looking the same" (4204-4205). That justification is false: formatValue for 'number' goes through toLocaleString with default grouping (format.ts:105-131, 9-19), whereas absent/plain format returns the raw string (format.ts:111-113), so '1234.5' changes from '1,234.5' to '1234.5'. More importantly the branch cannot tell an auto-added nf from a user-chosen one: with a cell value '1234.5' and user style {nf:'number', dp:1}, a decrease (writes dp:0 via 4213-4217) followed by an increase hits the branch (target=1===valueDp=1) and unsets dp AND nf, silently destroying the user's number format and grouping — contradicting the "leaves the selection exactly as they found it" invariant documented at 4188-4194. unsetRangeStyleKeys genuinely removes the key from the owning layer (4242-4310; behavior shown by decimals.test.ts:132-139). The existing test decimals.test.ts:141-160 only avoids this because decimalsInValue('12')===0. The reviewer's citation of decimals.test.ts:89-92 is partly mischaracterized (there the nf was auto-added, so that round trip is intended), but the underlying defect — loss of an explicit user number format / changed rendering — is real and reachable, an incorrect state update and silent style loss in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` (sheet.ts:4343-4373) rebuilds the cell with `compactCell(existing, next)` and writes it via `store.set`, which replaces rather than merges (memory.ts:97-100; yorkie-store.ts:259-290 -> worksheet-grid.ts:188-191). `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:57-69) copies only `v`, `f`, `s`, while `Cell` also carries `spillRows`/`spillCols`/`spillAnchor`/`spillBlocked` (types.ts:209-217), so those fields are erased. The path is user-reachable: spreadsheet.ts:536/546 -> `changeDecimals` -> sheet.ts:4208 `unsetRangeStyleKeys` -> sheet.ts:4334. The `if (!existing?.s) continue` early-out does not protect spill anchors, because the calculator writes anchors with a style plus spill metadata (calculator.ts:131-136, and the blocked branch at 118-125). Erasing `spillRows`/`spillCols` disables the ghost-cell cleanup gated on them at calculator.ts:74-85, leaving stale orphaned ghost cells and corrupting blocked state — a genuine correctness/data-integrity bug in this lens's lane. No guard elsewhere excludes spill cells from this path.
